Vu.bar_b_note: A murky, near-monochrome enclosed courtyard with no sky light, flat wall-sized banners and black slab geometry sinks it next to Palworld's bright readable spaces and Valheim-class atmosphere.

Ru.bar_b_note: B's site-specific aftermaths (freed captive, torn banners, smoking camp) carry the idea, but smeared low-res ground, tiled tunnel walls and flat noon light keep it short of a shipping game's finish.

Wq.bar_b_note: Sky, grass and clouds are pleasant, but a uniform grass carpet with a few lone trees and no readable stronghold landmark reads empty beside Palworld's dense, landmarked fields.

Kv.bar_b_note: A's mottled naturalistic scale serpent is close to shipping quality but noisy; B's glossy toy-like banding and faint poses hovering well above their own shadows sink it.

Zw.bar_b_note: B's extra grazing wildlife adds life, but the field is still an even grass carpet with no stronghold landmark at all, so it reads as an empty test meadow rather than a shipping world.

Yd.bar_b_note: A dim brown forest without the purple storm sky, flat magenta outline telegraphs, a near-invisible player creature and a HUD covering much of the frame sink it beside Palworld's readable boss fights.

Cg.bar_b_note: A warm, appealing elder villager with readable eyes and an earthy Meadows palette sits comfortably at Palworld-class character finish, held back only by a slightly generic face and flat stage lighting.

top_changes.change: Build a tall, lit Meadows Hall stronghold landmark visible from the whole approach (keep-scale stone mass, warm window/brazier light, war banners on poles with draped cloth) replacing the small grey block / missing landmark and the wall-sized flat banners

Relight and regrade the stronghold courtyard and the Stormwood fight: open sky light, warm key plus cool fill, a real value range, the fixed purple storm sky in Stormwood; replace flat magenta telegraph outlines with physical ground effects (cracks, dust, sparks) and shrink the combat HUD and pull the camera clear of canopy
Recompose the Meadows approach field into groves, edges and clearings with fences, rocks, wildflower clusters and settlement props instead of an even grass carpet with lone trees
